info.title: Yolt API
info.summary: Paste a YouTube link, get back its best moments as clips; search them by their words.
info.description:
Everything the Yolt UI does goes through this API. Submit a YouTube link as a **run**; Yolt fetches the video's captions or transcribes it with Parakeet, Highlightr picks the moments, and the run's **clips** become searchable alongside every other clip.

## Model

- **Episode**: a video. Created the first time a link to it is submitted.
- **Run**: one clipping job on an episode, with optional instructions and clip options. Every submission is a new run, with the same instructions and options or not, and reuses the video's transcript.
- **Transcript**: every word, timed. `/text` is the untimed text, `/words` the timed words, `/srt` captions.
- **Clip**: a span Highlightr picked, addressed by an inclusive word range. Clips never change once their run is ready. Each has a public `share_url`.
- **Compilation**: a lineage of immutable **revisions** sharing a title. Its ID is the ID of its first revision. A revision is an ordered list of items, each a clip and an inclusive word range; the server derives the times and the transcript. Revisions are created whole or not at all, and a new one must name the revision it's based on.
- **Speaker**: a person featured in an episode, as a host or guest. Inferred once per episode from the video's title, channel, description and opening minutes; `verified` is false until someone confirms it (`PUT /episodes/{episode_id}/speakers`). Speakers belong to episodes, not clips.
- **Subscription**: a YouTube channel Yolt checks for new uploads, finished livestreams, or both, every few hours (Settings). A check keeps the newest videos that are long enough; they're listed at `/subscriptions/videos`, and clipping one is an ordinary run. With `autoclip` on, each check queues a run for every new video it finds.
- **Render**: a record that a revision was rendered outside Yolt, so each clip's `usage` counts what shipped.

## Search

`q` on `/clips` is keyword search by default. `search=semantic` ranks every embedded clip by meaning, `search=hybrid` merges both rankings (recommended), and `like` finds clips similar to ones you pick. `/clips/facets` counts what `/clips` would return, and `/themes` clusters every clip by what is said in it. Clips are embedded after their run is ready, by the embedding server set in Settings; `GET /` reports coverage, and semantic search answers 503 when that server is unavailable. Keyword search always works.

## Feed

`GET /feed` picks clips to play one after another, like a TV channel (the UI's TV page). It favours clips made recently, by age tiers weighted in Settings (`feed_mix`), and clips the feed has played less; it never repeats a clip in a batch, skips the ones shown most recently (`recent`), and doesn't play two clips from one episode in a row while there are others. `POST /feed/plays` counts a play. It takes the same filters as `GET /clips`, so a channel can be a search, a theme, a speaker or unused clips.

## Labs

Experimental features built on semantic search, under `/labs`. `GET /labs` lists them; each can be switched off in Settings (`labs_disabled`), and then its endpoints answer 404 `lab-disabled`. Their shapes may change between versions.

## Conventions

- Times are integer milliseconds in the original video. Word ranges are inclusive: `{"first": 120, "last": 188}`.
- Lists use cursor pagination (`limit`, `cursor`, `next_cursor`).
- Errors use RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`. Every problem is listed at once, each with a `pointer` (into the body) or `parameter`, and a stable `code`.
- A query parameter the operation doesn't define is a `400 unknown_parameter`, never silently ignored. A single-value parameter sent twice is a 400 too. List parameters are repeated (`episode_id=1&episode_id=2`); `include` also takes a comma list.
- Text can't contain NUL (U+0000) or an unpaired surrogate (`"\ud800"`): a parameter with one is a `400 invalid_value` and a body string or member name with one a `422 invalid_value`. Like a body that isn't JSON, that's checked first and listed on its own.
- Bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`); anything else is a 415. Writes from another site's page are refused (403).
- The endpoint shapes follow the clipit catalogue API, so a client written for it needs a new base URL, not new code.

get.description: What the latest round of subscription checks found, and what's been clipped in the last `clipped.days` days. A round is the latest check and every check before it with no gap of more than 10 minutes between them; its new videos are the ones found during it.

post.summary: Retry a failed or cancelled run
post.description: A transcript that already finished is reused.

post.summary: Cancel a queued or processing run
post.description: The run is `cancelled` at once and keeps the stage it reached. The worker drops it at its next progress update and moves on to the next queued run: within a second or so while downloading, converting the audio or waiting on Highlightr, but only after Parakeet answers while transcribing (that request can't be interrupted; its transcript is kept for later runs). Highlightr isn't told, so a job it already started runs to the end there. Cancelling a cancelled run again returns it unchanged; `POST /runs/{run_id}/retry` queues it again.

get.summary: Get the complete transcript as plain text
get.description: The untimed `full_text` as UTF-8, intended for whole-episode reading. It can exceed 200,000 characters. `Range: bytes=…` is supported. Compute byte ranges from `Transcript.text_bytes`, not `text_chars`. A range that splits a multi-byte character is widened to the character boundary, and `Content-Range` reports the bytes actually sent. A malformed, reversed or multi-range header is ignored and the whole text is sent.

get.description: Caption rows built from the timed words: the same SRT Highlightr was given.

get.summary: Get timed words in an inclusive sequence range
get.description: Every word of a transcript is timed, numbered from 1 to `word_count`. A range past the end is a `422 words_missing`. A range can span at most 5,000 words.

parameters.name: last
parameters.description: Must be ≥ `first` and < `first` + 5000.

get.summary: Find clips
get.description:
With `q`, `q` selects or ranks clips, and each result carries the clip's complete `text` plus a `match` block. `search` picks how `q` is read:

- `keyword` (the default): full-text search over each clip's ~20-second passages. Only clips with a matching passage are returned.
- `semantic`: `q` is embedded and every embedded clip is ranked by meaning, so results needn't share a word with `q`. Use `min_similarity` to cut the tail.
- `hybrid`: both rankings merged by reciprocal rank fusion. Exact names and terms rank high, and so do paraphrases. Recommended for agents.

`like` ranks clips by similarity to one or more clips ("more like this") without embedding anything. It excludes the liked clips themselves.

Semantic results (`semantic`, `hybrid`, `like`) are ordered by `-relevance` only. Every other filter applies before ranking. Clips without a vector are invisible to semantic ranking; `GET /` reports coverage.

For supercuts, add `max_per_episode` to spread results across episodes, and `diversify=true` to avoid clips that repeat each other. `exclude_id` drops clips you already have, and `exclude_episode_id` whole episodes.

With `id`, returns exactly those clips, once each, in the order requested, and `next_cursor` is null. Other filters still apply. `limit`, `cursor`, `sort`, `diversify` and `max_per_episode` don't apply to a batch, so sending one is a 400.

For surveys, `view=compact` leaves out text and includes and allows `limit` up to 1000.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Repeatable, up to 200. Batch-fetch by clip ID.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: How `q` is read; see above. `semantic` and `hybrid` need `q`, limit it to 300 characters, and answer 503 when semantic search is unavailable.

parameters.name: like
parameters.description: Repeatable, up to 50. Rank by similarity to the mean of these clips' vectors. Can't be combined with `q`. An unknown clip is a 422 `clip_not_found`, and a clip without a vector a 422 `not_embedded`.

parameters.name: min_similarity
parameters.description: Only with `search=semantic`, `search=hybrid` or `like`. Drops clips whose `match.similarity` is lower (in hybrid, this includes keyword matches with no vector).

parameters.name: theme
parameters.description: Only clips in this theme, by its ID from `GET /themes` (such as `k30-1911-3fa2`). A malformed ID is a 400. An ID the current clustering doesn't have is a 422 `theme_not_found`: the vectors changed since it was listed.

parameters.name: usage
parameters.description: `never`: no revision has ever picked the clip (`usage.revisions == 0`). `picked`: at least one revision has (`usage.revisions > 0`). `rendered`: at least one recorded render contains it (`usage.rendered > 0`).

parameters.name: exclude_id
parameters.description: Repeatable, up to 200. Leave out these clips.

parameters.name: exclude_episode_id
parameters.description: Repeatable. Leave out clips from these episodes.

parameters.name: max_per_episode
parameters.description: At most this many clips per episode: the best ones by the current order, chosen across the whole result set, so pagination stays consistent. Works in every mode.

parameters.name: diversify
parameters.description: Only with `search=semantic`, `search=hybrid` or `like`. Re-ranks the best 200 candidates by maximal marginal relevance, so each next clip is relevant and also unlike the clips before it. Returns a single page of up to `limit`: `next_cursor` is null and `cursor` is a 400.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: A leading `-` means descending. Defaults to `-relevance` when `q` or `like` is set, otherwise `-score`. `-relevance` is the match ranking: full-text rank, similarity, or the fused hybrid score; it needs `q` or `like`, and semantic modes allow nothing else. `-created` is newest run first, best rank first within it. `-rendered` puts the most rendered clips first (then the most used in compilations).

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: `compact` returns `ClipSummary` objects: no `text`, includes or `match.passages`, and `limit` up to 1000. `include` is a 400 with it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 200, or 1000 with `view=compact`.

get.description:
Takes the same filters as `GET /clips` and counts the clips it would return, instead of listing them. Use it for broad questions: which episodes hold the most unused material on a subject (`group_by=episode&q=inflation&search=hybrid&min_similarity=0.45&sort=-unused`), or how much of the catalogue has never been picked (`group_by=usage`).

Semantic, hybrid and `like` ranking keep every embedded clip, so with them `min_similarity` is required: it decides what counts as a match.

get.summary: Get a clip
Get the transcript just before and after a clip
get.description: Use it to check whether a clip stands on its own or depends on an earlier question or setup.

get.summary: List every compilation revision and render that uses this clip
get.description: One entry per compilation item that uses the clip, so a revision that uses it twice appears twice.

get.summary: Get a clip by its share id
get.description: What a clip's public page (`share_url`) shows.

get.summary: Cluster the catalogue into themes
get.description:
Groups every embedded clip into `k` themes by what is said in it: spherical k-means over the mean of each clip's passage vectors (its own clip vector when it has no embedded passage), seeded, so the same vectors and `k` give the same themes. The API doesn't name themes: each has its most central clips (`representatives`) and distinctive `keywords`, so name it from those.

Use it to find fresh material: `sort=-unused` puts the themes with the most never-picked clips first, and `sort=coverage` the themes the fewest compilations draw on (at least 2 items each), then by unused clips. List a theme's clips with `GET /clips?theme={id}`, which takes every other filter too (`usage=never`, `view=compact`).

The clustering is computed once and cached until the vectors change; usage and coverage are read on every request.

A theme's ID is `k{k}-{most central clip}-{vectors}`, where the last part is four hex digits of the vectors' fingerprint, so an ID stops resolving as soon as the vectors change. Usage and coverage are live; `sort=-clips` and `-unused` match the sorts on `/clips/facets`.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: How many themes. Higher k gives narrower themes.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `-unused` (the default): most unused clips first. `-clips`: biggest first. `-cohesion`: tightest first. `coverage`: fewest covering compilations first, then most unused clips.

get.summary: Pick the next clips to play
get.description:
Picks up to `count` clips to play next, in order, each with its timed words for a live transcript.

Each pick chooses an age tier first, by the weights in Settings (`feed_mix`: clips made in the last 3, 7, 30 and 90 days, then any clip), skipping tiers with no clips, then a clip in it weighted by `1 / (1 + plays)²`, so clips the feed has played less come up more. A clip's age is when it was made, so a new run shows up straight away.

A batch never repeats a clip. It leaves out the `recent` clips and doesn't follow a clip with another from the same episode (starting with the last `recent` one); when the clips run out it relaxes the episode rule first, then `recent`, so it's shorter than `count` only when fewer clips match.

Takes the same filters as `GET /clips`: a feed can be a keyword or meaning search, a theme, a speaker, unused clips, and so on. Clips from runs that aren't ready are never picked.

parameters.name: min_similarity
parameters.description: Required with `search=semantic`, `search=hybrid` or `like`, which otherwise match every embedded clip: only clips at least this similar are in the feed.

parameters.name: theme

post.summary: Count a play of a clip in the feed
post.description: Call it when a clip starts playing in the feed. The feed favours clips it has played less (see `GET /feed`).

422.description: Not a valid body, or no such clip (`clip_not_found`).

post.summary: Review a draft compilation's items without saving
post.description: The one call for iterating on a draft. It resolves the items with every check a create runs (including overlaps, but not the title) and returns each one with its exact words, times and text, plus the transcript just before it, so a `follows_question` warning shows the question. It also reports editorial problems: repeated points, items that drift from the rest, cuts that start or end mid-sentence or leave out the question being answered, too many items from one episode or speaker, items too short (under 3 s) or too long (over half of `target_duration_ms`, or 90 s without one), and the total against the target. Nothing is saved, and the embedding server is never called. A create's dry run adds only the title check and the revision number.

get.summary: List compilation lineages, or find them by title or meaning

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Without `search` (or with `search=keyword`): web-search syntax over titles, like `q` elsewhere (quoted phrases, `or`, `-exclusions`; words are stemmed). With `search=semantic`: ranks lineages by meaning, at most 300 characters.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: `semantic` compares `q` with each lineage's vector: the mean of its latest revision's clip vectors. Use it to check whether a theme has been done already, whatever the title says. Lineages with no embedded clip are left out. Answers 503 when semantic search is unavailable.

parameters.name: min_similarity
parameters.description: With `search=semantic`, leave out lineages less similar than this.

parameters.name: clip_id
parameters.description: Lineages whose latest revision uses this clip.

200.description: A page of compilations: most recently revised first, or most similar first with `search=semantic`.

post.summary: Create a compilation and its first revision atomically
post.description: With `dry_run=true`, the server runs every check, including those that span segments, and returns a preview of the revision. Nothing is written. Titles identify compilations, so a title that's already in use returns `409 title_taken` with that compilation's ID. Add a revision to it instead.

200.description: Dry run: the revision that would be created.

201.description: Created. `Location` is the new revision's canonical URL, `/revisions/{revision_id}`.

get.summary: Get a compilation lineage

200.description: The lineage, with its latest revision summarized.

get.summary: List a lineage's revisions, oldest first

post.description: Send the complete new item list. `based_on` must equal the compilation's current latest revision number. If it does not, the server returns `409` with `latest_number`. The new revision keeps the compilation's title. Supports `dry_run`, like create.

200.description: Dry run: the revision that would be created.

get.summary: Redirect to a revision by its number in the lineage, or to the latest
get.description: Always returns `307` to `/revisions/{revision_id}`, carrying the query string with it. A redirect for a numbered revision may be cached. A redirect for `latest` is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

307.description: Redirect to the canonical revision URL.

get.summary: Get one revision with its fully resolved items
get.description: This is a revision's canonical URL. It returns everything review and rendering tools need in one call: clip, episode, source media, and text. `include=speakers` adds each item's speakers and `include=captions` its caption words. The response carries an `ETag` (it differs per `include`), and `If-None-Match` returns `304`.

get.summary: Compare a revision with another revision
get.description: Pairs items in two greedy, in-order passes. First, items with the same clip and the same words are paired. Then remaining items of the same clip whose words overlap are paired as re-trims. Each item pairs with the first unpaired match in the other revision. Anything left over is added or removed.

parameters.name: against
parameters.description: The revision ID to compare with. It defaults to the revision's `based_on` and can belong to another compilation. If the revision has no `based_on` and `against` is omitted, the request fails with `422 no_base_revision`.

get.summary: Review a saved revision's items
get.description: The same checks as `POST /segments/review`, on a saved revision. Use it before rendering, or to audit older compilations.

parameters.name: target_duration_ms
parameters.description: Flag a total more than 10% away from this.

get.summary: List recorded renders of a revision

post.description: Called by `produce.py render` after the output file has been written. Never call it for previews. Only the items listed in `positions` (all items if `positions` is omitted) count toward `usage.rendered`.

get.summary: List subscriptions, by channel name

post.description: Looks the channel up on YouTube, then checks it straight away in the background (`check_pending`). A channel you already follow returns its subscription with `200`, now following what this request asks for.

200.description: Already subscribed; now following what was asked.

422.description: `not_youtube` (not a channel or video link), `video_unavailable` (a video link YouTube couldn't look up), `channel_unavailable` (YouTube has no such channel, or couldn't be reached), or `nothing_followed`.

get.summary: Videos the checks found, newest first
get.description: Each check keeps a channel's three newest videos of each followed kind that are long enough (`subscription_min_minutes`) and not live, upcoming or members-only, looking at its 5 newest uploads and 25 newest livestreams.

parameters.name: podcast_id
parameters.description: Only these channels. Repeatable.

parameters.name: clipped
parameters.description: `true`: only videos with a queued, processing or ready run; `false`: only the rest.

get.summary: Export every subscription as a file
get.description: Every followed channel, by name, with what it follows and whether it auto-clips, as a JSON file (`Content-Disposition: attachment`) that `POST /subscriptions/import` reads back, here or in another Yolt. The videos found and check history aren't in it.

post.summary: Subscribe to every channel in an export file
post.description: Takes a file from `GET /subscriptions/export` as it is (or one written by hand: only `subscriptions[].channel_id` is required). YouTube isn't asked first, since the file names each channel by its id; each new subscription is checked in the background as usual, which refreshes its name and link. A channel you already follow is left as it is. All or nothing: if any entry is invalid, nothing is imported. A channel with `autoclip` on auto-clips from its first check on, as `POST /subscriptions` with `autoclip` does.

422.description: `invalid_value` (e.g. not a `UC…` channel id, a malformed handle, an unknown `format` or `version`), `unknown_field`, `missing_field`, or `nothing_followed`.

post.description: Marks every subscription as due. They're checked one at a time in the background; follow `check_pending` on each.

get.summary: Get a subscription

patch.summary: Change what a subscription follows, or its auto-clip
patch.description: Following a kind it didn't before checks the channel again straight away.

422.description: `nothing_followed`: it would follow neither uploads nor livestreams.

delete.description: The videos found so far stay in `/subscriptions/videos`.

post.description: Marks this subscription as due, after any already asked for, e.g. to retry a failed check without checking every channel. Follow `check_pending`.

get.summary: Get the service settings
get.description: Service endpoints and clipping preferences.

put.description: Omitted keys are unchanged; an empty string puts a key back to its default. Keys set by environment variables are read-only (`409 locked`).

post.description: Whether a Parakeet or Highlightr URL answers its /health endpoint, an LLM endpoint answers a one-line chat completion, or an embeddings URL returns a 1024-dimension vector. A failure is `ok: false`, not an error status.

get.summary: List the labs
get.description: Every lab, whether it's switched on, and whether the UI badges it as new.

get.summary: Thread an idea into an ordered reel
get.description: The clips that best match `q` by words and meaning (what `GET /clips?search=hybrid&diversify=true` returns, at most `max_per_episode` per episode), ordered so each leads into the next: the best match opens, then each next clip is the remaining one most like the one before it. A clip that overlaps a better one is left out, so `clips` is always a valid compilation: `review` is what `POST /segments/review` says about it, and `POST /compilations` with `items: [{clip_id}, …]` in this order saves it. Nothing is saved here.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The idea.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many clips, at most.

parameters.name: max_per_episode
parameters.description: At most this many clips from one episode.

parameters.name: usage
parameters.description: `never`: only clips no compilation has used.

parameters.name: target_duration_ms
parameters.description: The length the review checks against, as in `POST /segments/review`.

post.summary: Delete every episode, clip and compilation
post.description: Clears the catalogue for a fresh start: every episode, transcript, run (queued and processing ones too), clip with its thumbnail and vectors, compilation with its revisions and render records, speaker and TV play. Subscriptions, the videos they found (now not clipped) and Settings stay; auto-clip doesn't queue the videos it queued before again. A run in progress stops as if cancelled. Can't be undone.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: Opaque value from `next_cursor`. Only valid with the same filters and sort that produced it. Otherwise, or if it was altered, the request fails with 400.

compilation_id.name: compilation_id
compilation_id.description: The ID of the compilation's first revision. Any other revision ID returns 404.

number.name: number
number.description: The revision's number within its lineage (1, 2, …) or `latest`.

BadRequest.description: An unknown query parameter (`unknown_parameter`), or a malformed or out-of-range query, path or header parameter (including an unknown `include` or `sort` value), a body that isn't valid JSON, or a cursor that doesn't match the request.

Invalid.description: The request was well formed but failed validation. Every problem is listed, in two stages: schema problems (unknown fields, wrong types, missing or reversed values) first, and only when there are none, the checks that need the catalogue (clips, word ranges, anchors, overlaps).

errors.message: Word 10412 is past the clip's last word (10390).
'you know' occurs 4 times in clip 97; add more words.
Times and transcript are derived from words; send `words` instead.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the resource's current state.

Forbidden.description: A write from another site's page (its `Origin` isn't this server).

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The body isn't JSON. Send `Content-Type: application/json`.

RangeNotSatisfiable.description: The byte range is outside the text.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Semantic search is unavailable: the problem `type` ends in `embedding-unavailable` when no embedding server is set or it didn't answer, and in `vectors-unavailable` when no clip has a vector from the current model yet. Keyword search keeps working.

CompilationConflict.description: `based_on` is not the latest revision number, or the title is already used by another compilation. `errors` names the field (`/title` or `/based_on`) like any other problem; the top-level `code` and the fields below are kept for the specific case.

compilation_id.description: Present when `code` is `title_taken`: the existing compilation.

queue.description: Runs waiting and running. One run is processed at a time.

embeddings.description: What semantic search can see. `like` needs vectors; `search=semantic` and `search=hybrid` also need `query_embedding` to be `configured`.

model.description: The `model_name` vectors must carry to be compared.

query_embedding.description: Whether Settings name an embedding server. Its reachability isn't checked here.

pending_clips.description: Clips not yet searchable by meaning: they or one of their passages have no vector from `model`. The worker embeds a run's clips right after it's ready and catches up on the rest when idle.

last_error.description: Why the latest embedding attempt failed, or which inputs the server refused and are being skipped (until this server restarts or the embedding settings change); `null` once an attempt succeeds with nothing skipped. The worker retries every few minutes.

embedded.description: Rows with a vector from the configured model. The rest are invisible to semantic search.

stale.description: Always 0: a clip's text never changes once it's stored. Kept so clients reading it keep working.

embedded.description: Rows with a vector from the configured model. The rest are invisible to semantic search.

stale.description: Embedded rows whose text changed since; they still rank, by their old text, until the worker re-embeds them.

pointer.description: A JSON Pointer into the request body.

parameter.description: The name of the query, path, or header parameter at fault.

code.description: Stable and machine-readable. This is an open set: clients must tolerate codes not listed in `x-known-values`.

WordRange.description: An inclusive range of transcript word sequence numbers. `last` must be ≥ `first` (`words_reversed`).

Source.description: Where media can be fetched from. The catalogue stores no file paths.

Usage.description: How often a clip has been used.

compilations.description: Distinct lineages whose latest revision uses the clip.

revisions.description: Revisions of any lineage that use the clip, including superseded ones.

rendered.description: Recorded renders whose `positions` include an item that uses this clip.

EpisodeInfo.description: An episode reference plus where the video lives and how long it is.

duration_ms.description: Null when YouTube doesn't report a length (e.g. a live stream).

Episode.description: A video. It's created the first time a link to it is submitted.

subscription.description: The subscription to its channel, if any. Subscribe with `POST /subscriptions` and the channel's `podcast_url`.

speakers.description: Hosts first. Empty until speakers are inferred, or if nobody was identified.

transcripts.description: Transcripts with at least one run, newest run first.

clip_count.description: Clips across all of its runs.

embedded_clip_count.description: How many of those clips are searchable by meaning (they and their passages have vectors from the configured model). Fewer than `clip_count` means some are still waiting; see `GET /` for why.

match.description: Present only when the request used `q`.

snippets.description: Short excerpts with matched terms wrapped in «…».

source.description: Parakeet, the creator's YouTube captions, or YouTube's auto-generated captions.

word_count.description: Every word is kept and timed: `/words` covers 1…`word_count`.

punctuated.description: Whether the text marks sentence ends: at least 1 per 100 words. YouTube's auto-captions don't, so cut-point checks are skipped for them.

text_chars.description: Unicode code points in the full text. Use it to estimate reading cost.

text_bytes.description: UTF-8 bytes in the full text. Use it to compute `Range` requests.

watch.description: The video on YouTube, starting at the clip.

embed.description: A YouTube embed limited to the clip's span.

video_thumbnail.description: YouTube's thumbnail for the whole video.

Clip.description: A span of a video Highlightr picked. Clips never change once their run is ready.

run_id.description: The run that produced the clip.

rank.description: Rank within its run; 1 is Highlightr's strongest pick.

source.description: The video the clip is in.

text.description: The complete text of the clip.

speakers.description: Only with `include=speakers`: everyone featured in the clip's episode. The catalogue doesn't record who says which clip.

details.description: Only with `include=details`: the raw Highlightr clip (scores, headlines, quotes, hashtags, category).

thumbnail_url.description: A frame from the clip, or the video's thumbnail when there's none.

match.description: Present when the request used `q` or `like`. Keyword search sets `relevance`. Semantic search and `like` set `similarity`. Hybrid sets all three, and `relevance` or `similarity` is null when the clip isn't in that list.

relevance.description: Full-text rank. Present with `search=keyword` (never null) and `search=hybrid`.

similarity.description: Present with semantic, hybrid and `like`; null for a passage with no vector.

passages.description: Keyword: every passage that matched, in transcript order. Semantic and `like`: the 3 nearest passages, nearest first. Hybrid: the 3 nearest plus any keyword match.

similarity.description: Cosine similarity, from -1 to 1: the best of the clip's own vector and its passages' vectors. Present with `search=semantic`, `like` (never null) and `search=hybrid`.

fused.description: Hybrid only: the reciprocal rank fusion score, `1/(60 + keyword rank) + 1/(60 + semantic rank)`, with ranks over the whole catalogue.

ClipSummary.description: A clip without its text, for `view=compact`.

run_id.description: The run that produced the clip.

rank.description: Rank within its run; 1 is Highlightr's strongest pick.

source.description: The video the clip is in.

thumbnail_url.description: A frame from the clip, or the video's thumbnail when there's none.

match.description: Present when the request used `q` or `like`: `Clip.match` without `passages`.

relevance.description: Full-text rank. Present with `search=keyword` (never null) and `search=hybrid`.

similarity.description: Cosine similarity, from -1 to 1: the best of the clip's own vector and its passages' vectors. Present with `search=semantic`, `like` (never null) and `search=hybrid`.

fused.description: Hybrid only: the reciprocal rank fusion score, `1/(60 + keyword rank) + 1/(60 + semantic rank)`, with ranks over the whole catalogue.

before.description: Up to `before_words` words before the clip.

after.description: Up to `after_words` words after the clip.

alignment.description: Always `exact` in Yolt, which keeps every timed word. Kept for clients written against clipit.

starts_mid_sentence.description: A heuristic: the text before the clip doesn't end with sentence punctuation. Null when the transcript has no punctuation (YouTube auto-captions), where it can't be told.

follows_question.description: A heuristic: the text before the clip ends with a question, which the clip may depend on. Null when the transcript has no punctuation (YouTube auto-captions), where it can't be told.

Run.description: One clipping job: a video plus instructions. Runs are processed one at a time, oldest first.

instructions.description: What the clips should focus on, sent to Highlightr as its style. Empty means Highlightr's default.

options.description: The clip options this run was given; empty when it follows Settings.

stage.description: While processing (and where a failed or cancelled run stopped). `captions` means YouTube's own transcript is used, so `downloading` and `transcribing` are skipped.

step.description: The step within `identifying`: `waiting` (Highlightr is busy with other jobs), `discovering` (window by window; `progress` and `detail` count them), `ranking` (every candidate together), `writing_headlines`, then Yolt `saving` the clips (`progress` counts them). Highlightr reports no progress within ranking and headlines, so `step_started_at` shows how long it has been on one.

progress.description: 0–1 within the current stage, when known.

attempts.description: How many times the worker has started it.

oneOf.description: Parakeet, the creator's YouTube captions, or YouTube's auto-generated captions.

embedded_clip_count.description: How many of this run's clips are searchable by meaning (they and their passages have vectors from the configured model). Fewer than `clip_count` means some are still waiting; see `GET /` for why.

finished_at.description: When it became ready, failed or was cancelled.

clips.description: Only with `include=clips`: its clips, best rank first.

url.description: A YouTube link or an 11-character video ID.

instructions.description: What the clips should focus on. Omit or leave blank for the default from Settings.

channel_id.description: Its channel's `UC…` id, when YouTube gives one. Then `POST /subscriptions` with this video's link subscribes to that channel.

subscription.description: The subscription to its channel, if any.

creator.description: Language of creator-uploaded captions in the spoken language, if any.

auto.description: Language of auto-generated captions in the spoken language, if any.

transcript_source.description: What a new run would use, with the current settings.

runs.description: Runs already made on this video, newest first.

values.description: Effective values: a key with nothing saved is its default. Secrets are always blank. Only an environment variable set to empty makes a value empty.

defaults.description: What each key is when nothing is saved for it (the settings form shows these as placeholders).

env_overrides.description: Keys set by environment variables; they can't be changed here.

youtube_captions.description: Use YouTube's transcript instead of Parakeet when available: creator or auto-generated (`any`, the default), creator-uploaded only (`manual`), or never (`off`). Auto-captions have no punctuation, so cut-point checks are skipped for them.

llm_api_key.description: Omit to keep, empty string to clear.

embed_url.description: An OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` URL. Semantic search is off when this URL is empty (the default).

embed_model.description: Vectors record their model, so changing it makes every clip pending again; the worker re-embeds them.

max_clips.description: The most clips a run keeps (whole number above 0, default 8).

candidates_per_window.description: Candidates Highlightr proposes per discovery window (1–10, default 3) before ranking them all together.

clip_instructions.description: Default clip focus for new links.

subscription_check_hours.description: Hours between checks of each subscription, 0 to 168 (default 24). 0 checks only when asked (`POST /subscriptions/check`) or on subscribing.

subscription_min_minutes.description: The shortest video a subscription check keeps, in minutes, 0 to 600 (default 30).

labs_disabled.description: Labs to switch off, as a comma list of their IDs from `GET /labs` (`thread,foryou`). Empty switches every lab on.

feed_mix.description: The TV feed's weights for clips made in the last 3, 7, 30 and 90 days, then for any clip: five whole numbers from 0 to 100, separated by commas, at least one above 0 (default `50,30,10,5,5`).

model.description: `llm` and `embeddings` only. Omit to use the saved model.

api_key.description: `llm` only. Omit to use the saved key, empty string to send none.

processing.description: Runs being processed now: one, or none when the queue is idle.

totals.description: What the UI's sidebar counts, polled along with the queue.

episodes.description: Episodes with at least one run, whatever its status.

group_count.description: Groups with at least one match; `groups` holds up to `limit`.

key.description: Episode or speaker ID, or `never`, `picked_unrendered` or `rendered`.

label.description: Episode title or speaker name; for usage, the same as `key`.

unused_count.description: Of those, how many no revision has ever picked (`usage=never`).

keywords.description: Words frequent in this theme's titles and summaries and rare in other themes.

representatives.description: The clips nearest the theme's centre.

unused_count.description: Clips no revision has ever picked (`usage=never`).

cohesion.description: Mean similarity of its clips to its centre: higher is tighter. Only comparable between themes of one clustering.

coverage.description: How much existing compilations already use the theme. A compilation covers it when at least 2 items of its latest revision come from the theme's clips.

compilation_count.description: Compilations covering the theme. 0 means nothing has been made from it yet.

compilations.description: The covering compilations with the most items from the theme, most first.

item_count.description: Items of its latest revision from the theme.

tier.description: The age tier it was picked through. `all_time` is every clip, whatever its age.

plays.description: How many times the feed had played it before.

words.description: The clip's timed words, in order, for a live transcript.

candidates.description: How many clips matched the filters: what the feed picks from.

plays.description: Plays in the feed so far, this one included.

SegmentSelection.description: Which part of a clip to use. Send only `clip_id` for the whole clip, add `words` for an exact trim, or add `text` to trim by phrase. The server resolves times and the transcript version. A compilation can use the same clip more than once. No two items may share a word: items from the same transcript must not overlap, even when they come from different clips (`overlapping_segments`).

TextAnchors.description: Trims from the first word of `from` to the last word of `to`. Matching runs on normalized word tokens: case and punctuation are ignored, and caption fixes are not applied. `from` must occur exactly once in the clip. `to` is searched only after the end of `from`, and must occur exactly once in that remainder. It may not overlap `from`. Omit either phrase to keep the clip's own boundary. Without `from`, `to` must occur exactly once in the whole clip.

Caption.description: One timed word. Times are relative to the start of its item. `at_ms` is 0 for the item's first word.

RevisionStats.description: These values change over time. They are kept separate from the revision's content, which never changes.

compilation_id.description: The compilation's ID: the ID of its first revision.

based_on.description: The previous revision's number. Null for revision 1.

created_at.description: When the revision was saved. Null for revisions saved before creation times were recorded.

RevisionPreview.description: The result of a dry run. Nothing was saved.

number.description: The number the revision would get.

retrimmed.description: The same clip with different but overlapping words.

moved.description: Identical items whose order relative to the others changed: the pairs outside the longest order-preserving chain. Items that only shifted because of an insert or removal aren't listed.

id.description: The ID of its first revision.

title.description: Titles identify compilations: every revision shares it.

similarity.description: Cosine similarity of `q` and the lineage's vector.

based_on.description: Must equal the lineage's current latest revision number.

format.description: `long` is 16:9; `short` is vertical and under 60 s.

positions.description: The item positions this render used. Omit it when the render used all of them. Positions past the end of the revision are rejected (`positions_out_of_range`).
Always populated. When the request omitted `positions`, it lists every item.

render_ids.description: Renders of this revision whose `positions` include this item.

Review.description: Editorial checks on an ordered list of items. Findings advise; nothing is rejected. `warning` findings usually need a fix before rendering; `info` findings are worth a look.

findings.description: Warnings first, then infos. Within each, findings about the whole list come first, then by position.

code.description:
An open set: tolerate codes not listed in `x-known-values`.

- `near_duplicate`: two items (not cuts of one clip) are very similar, so they may make the same point.
- `off_theme`: an item is much less similar to the rest than the compilation's typical item. A weak signal.
- `starts_mid_sentence`, `ends_mid_sentence`: the cut isn't on a sentence boundary.
- `follows_question`: the item answers a question that comes just before it and isn't included.
- `episode_heavy`, `speaker_heavy`: more than 40% (and at least 3) of the items come from one episode, or from episodes featuring one speaker. Speakers are attributed per episode.
- `duration_off_target`: the total is more than 10% from `target_duration_ms`.
- `item_too_short`, `item_too_long`: under 3 s, or over half of `target_duration_ms` (90 s without one).
- `cut_points_unchecked` (info): these items come from a transcript without punctuation (YouTube auto-captions), so `starts_mid_sentence`, `ends_mid_sentence` and `follows_question` weren't checked for them.

positions.description: The items concerned. Empty for findings about the whole list.

similarity.description: For `near_duplicate` (between the two items) and `off_theme` (to the rest).

skipped.description: Checks that couldn't run: `near_duplicate` and `off_theme` need the catalogue's vectors.

text.description: The item's own words, as it will be heard.

before.description: The dozen or so words of the transcript just before the item.

alignment.description: How the item was located in the full transcript. With `approximate`, the boundary checks may be off by a few words.

theme_similarity.description: Cosine similarity to the mean of the other items. An item's vector is the mean of its passages within the trimmed range, else its clip's. Null without vectors, or with fewer than 3 embedded items.

starts_mid_sentence.description: Null when the item's transcript has no punctuation.

follows_question.description: Null when the item's transcript has no punctuation.

ends_mid_sentence.description: Null when the item's transcript has no punctuation.

segments.description: The draft's items, in order, exactly as they would be sent to create a compilation.

RevisionMetadata.description: Free-form context for a revision, stored as given: for example the theme, the search query, or a note on each item. A JSON object of at most 16384 bytes. Defaults to `{}`.

verified.description: If false, the attribution is a guess. Don't name this person on screen.

verified_count.description: Of those, how many someone confirmed.

SpeakersUpdate.description: The episode's complete list of speakers. They're stored as verified, and inference won't replace them.

Subscription.description: A followed YouTube channel. Its channel is the same podcast that episodes from it name (`podcast_id`).

podcast_id.description: The channel, as `podcast_id` filters name it elsewhere.

uploads.description: Follows the channel's uploads (its Videos tab).

streams.description: Follows its finished livestreams (its Live tab). Live and upcoming streams are skipped until they end.

autoclip.description: Auto-clip: each check queues a run, with the default instructions (`clip_instructions`), for every video found since this was turned on that has no run yet. A video is auto-clipped once at most: one whose run failed or was cancelled isn't queued again by itself. The runs join the one queue like any other.

autoclip_since.description: When auto-clip was turned on; videos found before that aren't auto-clipped. Null when it's off.

checked_at.description: When the last check finished, whether or not it worked.

check_error.description: Why the last check failed. A failed scheduled check is retried after 1 and then 5 minutes.

check_pending.description: A check is due: just subscribed, newly following a kind, asked for (`POST /subscriptions/check`, or `/subscriptions/{id}/check` for one), or the interval has passed. The server checks one channel at a time.

next_check_at.description: When the next check is due; null when scheduled checks are off (`subscription_check_hours` is 0) and none was asked for.

video_count.description: Videos found on this channel so far.

unclipped_count.description: Of those, the ones without a queued, processing or ready run.

url.description: A channel URL (`/@handle`, `/channel/UC…`, `/c/…`, `/user/…`), an `@handle`, a `UC…` channel id, or a link to one of the channel's videos (any YouTube video link, or its 11-character id): the channel it's on is followed.

autoclip.description: Auto-clip what the checks find (see `Subscription.autoclip`), from its first check on. Omitted: off for a new subscription, unchanged for one you already follow.

SubscriptionUpdate.description: Omitted keys are unchanged. At least one of `uploads` and `streams` must end up true.

autoclip.description: Turning it on auto-clips the videos found from now on, not the ones found already.

pending.description: Subscriptions now waiting for a check.

SubscriptionExport.description: An export file of every subscription.

subscriptions.description: A channel listed more than once is imported as first listed.

name.description: Used until the first check, if Yolt doesn't know the channel yet. Omitted: the channel id.

url.description: Ignored: the link is rebuilt from `channel_id`, and the first check sets the channel's own.

created.description: New subscriptions, each now waiting for its first check.

already_subscribed.description: Channels already followed, left as they were.

ChannelVideo.description: A video a subscription check found. It stays after an unsubscribe.

url.description: Its watch URL; `POST /runs` with it to clip it.

published_at.description: As precise as the channel page gives it when first seen ("3 days ago" is a day); the episode has the exact time once clipped.

episode_id.description: Set once the video has been submitted.

run.description: Its run: one still going, else a ready one, else the latest. Null if never submitted.

id.description: Used in `labs_disabled` and in the lab's paths (`/labs/{id}`).

new.description: Whether the UI badges it as new.

clips.description: In thread order. Each has `match`, as with `GET /clips?search=hybrid`.

hops.description: The cosine similarity of each clip to the next (one fewer than `clips`); null when either has no vector.

subscriptions.description: The latest round of subscription checks.

last_checked_at.description: When its last check finished; null before any check.

new_videos.description: Videos it found that weren't known before.

clipped.description: Runs that finished (ready) in the last `days` days.

RunOptions.description: A run's own clip options. Each overrides the setting of the same name for this run, with the same rules; one left out follows Settings. The shortest clip can't be longer than the longest, counting the settings for any left out.

max_clips.description: The most clips the run keeps.

candidates_per_window.description: Candidates Highlightr proposes per 10-minute window before ranking them all together.

confirm.description: Must be `clear`, so a stray request can't delete everything.

ClearedCatalogue.description: What there was before it was deleted.

episodes.description: Episodes deleted, with their transcripts and speakers.

runs.description: Runs deleted, queued and processing ones included.

clips.description: Clips deleted, with their vectors and TV plays.

compilations.description: Compilations deleted, every revision and render record of each.
